summary: In January 2021 Dresden announced a three-step increase in on-street parking fees, the first in about 15 years, with further steps due in 2022 and 2023; these are on-street zone rates, not garage prices. After part of the Carolabruecke collapsed on 11 September 2024, figures reported in March 2025 showed higher traffic on other Elbe crossings. In 2019 and 2022 the city set out public charging expansion plans, including a 2022 forecast of 400 charge points by the end of 2022.

items.text: ADAC Sachsen commented on the city administration's plan to raise parking fees, which it said would be the first rise since 2006. It described the proposal as at least a doubling and up to 400 percent in some zones, and said it went too far.
items.source_title: ADAC Sachsen: Parken in Dresden darf nicht zum Luxus werden

items.text: The city announced a three-step increase in on-street parking fees, the first in 15 years, with the first step to follow the council's adoption of the fee ordinance in 2021 and further steps on 1 January 2022 and 1 January 2023. Hourly rates were 2.10 euros (zone 1) and 1.50 euros (zone 2) in 2021, 2.40 and 1.80 in 2022, and 2.70 and 2.10 in 2023, with day tickets of 12 and 6 euros from 2021; these are on-street zone rates, not garage prices.
items.source_title: Dresden erhöht die Parkgebühren erstmals nach 15 Jahren

items.text: A search-engine summary of a February 2019 city press release says Dresden introduced cashless payment by smartphone (E-Parkschein) at about 450 of its parking machines.
items.source_title: Dresden city press release (pm_003), February 2019, as shown in search results
items.unconfirmed_reason: The city's website was unavailable when we checked, so we could not read the press release.

items.text: APCOA's page for its Dresden-Mitte garage (Magdeburger Strasse 1) lists 606 spaces, a parking guidance system and ticketless parking through its FLOW app. It also lists 1.50 euros per hour with an 8 euro daily maximum for 08:00-20:00, as shown when checked in October 2026.

The city counted 163 public charging stations in August 2019 and planned over 400 normal and fast charging stations by 2022; the plan also includes more than 30 mobility points. The article does not mention parking garages.
items.source_title: Dresden kündigt massiven Ausbau der Ladeinfrastruktur an (electrive)

items.text: A city official said Dresden expected to reach 400 public charge points by the end of 2022 rather than the originally planned 2025, and that about 30 percent of public charging infrastructure was fast chargers. This was a forecast at the time of publication, not a result.
items.source_title: Dresden peilt Ladeinfrastruktur-Ziel drei Jahre früher an (electrive)

items.text: A search-engine summary says the city council adopted the Air Quality Plan 2017 on 24 January 2019, and that it includes parking management with a focus on residents around Schillerplatz in Blasewitz.
items.source_title: Landeshauptstadt Dresden: Parken Schillerplatz (archive page) and Luftreinhalteplan 2017 status report, as shown in search results
items.unconfirmed_reason: The city's website was unavailable when we checked, so we could not read the page, and we could not confirm that the measure has been implemented.

items.text: A search-engine summary of the city's page on the Altmarkt renovation says work began in April 2022.
items.source_title: Landeshauptstadt Dresden: Altmarkt (Sanierung), as shown in search results
items.unconfirmed_reason: The city's website was unavailable when we checked. The end date, and whether the work finished on schedule, are unconfirmed.

items.text: A section of the Carolabruecke collapsed into the Elbe on 11 September 2024; more than 30,000 vehicles a day had used the bridge, and tram tracks ran over the collapsed section. The last remains of the collapsed section were removed in May 2025 and demolition of the remaining standing parts followed from June, with the work described as almost complete about a year after the collapse.
items.source_title: Verkehrsinfrastruktur: Bilanz und Ausblick ein Jahr nach Carolabrücken-Einsturz (Logistik Heute)

items.text: Six months after the collapse, t-online reported Albertbruecke traffic up 88 percent, Marienbruecke up 30 percent and Waldschloesschenbruecke up 8 percent. North-south trips took about four minutes longer on average. DVB reported its highest passenger numbers since reunification in December 2024.
items.source_title: Dresden: So hat sich der Verkehr seit Einsturz der Carolabrücke verlagert (t-online)
